subject: Physical cross-connects & internal routing sanity check for private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: ops-engineering@acme-cloud.com
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Crossconnects: on-site cable mapping and routing validation

Neha / Jonas,

Thanks for walking the team through the initial topology yesterday. The colo ops crew started running their wiring checks this morning and surfaced two items we want to validate before we schedule the final handoff: 1) the intended spine-to-tunnel crossconnect pairs in Rack 14 and 2) the expected BGP next-hops for the tenant-facing VRF slices.

I've attached the cable diagram the colo provided (cablediagram_v2.png) and their checklist. Can you confirm the pin mappings and whether our control-plane management subnet is correctly isolated from tenant data lanes? If there's a short checklist we can hand them, that would speed the on-site verification.

High-level ask: can we confirm whether the planned crossconnects require any L2 stitching in the fabric, or if everything stays in routed L3 (i.e., no additional MAC learning or flood domains)?

Thanks,
Sarah Lee
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Corp
(attachment: cablediagram_v2.png image/png)
(attachment: crossconnect-checklist.xlsx application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, ops-engineering@acme-cloud.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Crossconnects: on-site cable mapping and routing validation

Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. Quick answers up front:

- Control plane management subnet must remain on a separate VRF (mgmt-VRF) and should not be reachable from tenant VRFs at L2. We expect pure L3 boundaries between tenant lanes and mgmt.
- For Rack 14 crossconnects, the pin mapping in cablediagram_v2.png looks correct except the labeled pair on Patch Panel 14B (ports 17/18) — colo swapped the pair order in their doc vs. our expected numbering. See inline comment below.

Action items I propose:
1) Jonas to confirm the BGP next-hop set for tenant slices and provide the small text snippet we can hand to colo.
2) I will publish a 1-page verification checklist (runbook-diff.txt) that explicitly calls out VRF isolation checks, BGP neighbor validation, and optical light/LOS checks.
3) On-site run: request a single test tenant route advertisement to validate route-suppression and verify no MAC learning on the management VLAN.

Cc'ing Jonas and Irene for the BGP and routing sanity checks.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
(attachment referenced: runbook-diff.txt text/plain)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Crossconnects: on-site cable mapping and routing validation

Thanks — I ran the BGP snippet against the staging fabric this morning. TL;DR: the planned next-hop set is fine for the tenant slices, but we need to ensure two small config items on the leaf peers:

- soft-reconfiguration inbound is enabled for the tenant peers (to avoid missing path attributes on partial updates).
- the mgmt-VRF export policy must not leak to the tenant export-policy; verify route-target filters.

Suggested handoff text for colo (one-liner they can paste into their config):

  neighbor 10.200.14.2 remote-as 65520
  address-family ipv4 vrf tenant-A
    next-hop-self
    soft-reconfiguration inbound

I'll attach a quick diff of the expected BGP neighbor block to the checklist (attachment: runbook-diff.txt). Marcus — can you sanity-check the routing adjacency numbers Jonas referenced against the Rack 14 patch numbering?

-Jonas
Lead Networks Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.com <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>

Date: 2026-11-21T17:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Crossconnects: on-site cable mapping and routing validation

Forwarding the colo ops response after they did a passive continuity check. Note the quoted response from the on-site tech below — they confirmed the physical ends but flagged that port labeling at the panel uses a vendor convention that inverts odd/even port numbering.

Continuity verified for the fiber pairs. Observed that Panel 14B labeling uses an alternate scheme and the cable swaps you noted correspond to how the vendor maps TX/RX when cabled in-field. We recommend swapping the patch order at the ODF so the pinned map aligns with your diagram.

Quick routing sanity snippet and an ops checklist entry:

- Confirmed: Rack 14 leaf pair IPs: 10.200.14.2/30 and 10.200.14.6/30 (tenant-VRF adjacencies).
- Confirmed: mgmt-VRF uses 10.254.14.0/24 and is not advertised to tenant VRFs.

Checklist item to hand to colo (one line to check):
  "Verify ODF patch order and confirm no L2 patching between mgmt and tenant panels; run BGP session test with soft-reconfig and advertise a single /24 from test-tenant to validate no leakage."

I also updated the runbook-diff.txt with the corrected port mapping for Patch Panel 14B. Attaching updated checklist.

Marcus Lin

Subject: Re: Crossconnects: on-site cable mapping and routing validation — confirmation and next steps

Fantastic — thanks everyone. Final notes and next steps:

1) Sarah / Acme ops: please have the field tech reorder the ODF patch for Panel 14B to match the port numbering on our diagram. Once done, please reply with a time window for a 15-minute test run.
2) Jonas & Marcus: I'll need the exact two-line BGP snippet (finalized) and the route-target filter text in the doc form so Acme can paste into their configuration system.
3) Irene: please add the confirmation that no L2 bridging occurs in the updated runbook-diff.txt.

If we get the test window today we'll run the advertisement, confirm no mgmt bleed, and then sign off the crossconnects and schedule the control-plane handover.

Neha Kapoor
